title: a review is not refused because main moved while it waited for CI: the check after the CI wait binds the reviewed head and base name, not the base tip, and every refusal there says why
acceptance: Why. On 2026-10-05 two review rounds ended `exit 65` with no verdict, no stderr line and no review_failed event before the reviewer adapter ever ran: reviewer-nikhil-t208-r2 (PR #195, head 2cc0380, launched while T-206 was merging) and reviewer-nikhil-t209-r2 (PR #198, head 050cc50, launched while T-210 was merging); each run's orchestration-result.json shows process_exit 65 with adapter_result status 'unknown' and no vendor, and /tmp/fm-review-T-20{8,9}.log hold only the actor and fm-vendor lines. Firstmate had to run `gh pr update-branch`, fast-forward the task worktree and relaunch by hand each time. Cause, read on main ddac6e0: bin/fm-review.sh sets REVIEW_PR_BASE and REVIEW_PR_BASE_HEAD at :312-316 just after the start check (:311), computes the reviewed head/merge-base/patch-id at :382-389, then calls `required_names; ci_wait` (:818), which waits up to FM_REVIEW_CI_WAIT seconds (default 1200, :626-633) for the head's required checks, and then calls `verify_review_head` again (:819). With REVIEW_PR_BASE set, that call (:303-309) runs `fm_binding head`, whose verified_base (bin/lib/fm_binding.py:266-276) requires the local base ref to equal the live base tip, and then compares `git rev-parse $REVIEW_PR_BASE^{commit}` with REVIEW_PR_BASE_HEAD; when main moved during the CI wait (a merge, then firstmate's fast-forward of the engine checkout) the base branch of the second clause differs and the function returns 65 from :307-308 without printing anything, and :819 exits without an event. A freshly pushed head always has CI running, so the CI wait is routinely many minutes long and any merge to main in that window voids the round before it starts. T-201 already made the final check (:1253, `verify_review_head final` → `fm_binding review-final`, fm_binding.py:130-149) bind only the reviewed head, fetched PR head, local task ref, open state and base name, because the reviewed merge-base and patch-id (:382-389) are pinned before the wait and gate 7 alone decides whether a verdict covers a later head (fm_evidence gate carry). The check after the CI wait guards the same thing as the final check and has no reason to be stricter.

Not the fix, and why. The PR being BEHIND is not what fm-review checks: neither the start check nor :819 reads mergeStateStatus, and a BEHIND PR reviews correctly (the diff is R_BASE..R_HEAD; gate 7 carries an APPROVE across a later merge of main with the same patch, T-113/T-201). Updating the branch from fm-review would change the head under review and needs GitHub write credentials, which rounds do not have (credential option A); the autopilot already updates BEHIND branches with compare-and-swap when no round is live (T-190, bin/lib/fm_autopilot_branches.py). So this task does not add a branch update anywhere; it removes the base-tip requirement from the check that runs after the CI wait.

The change, in bin/fm-review.sh only. (1) The call after the CI wait (:819) becomes `verify_review_head settled`. In verify_review_head (:288-310), the argument value `settled` takes exactly the path `final` takes today (`fm_binding review-final --task --pr --branch --head "$R_HEAD" --base-name "$REVIEW_PR_BASE"`, then compare its output with R_HEAD); `final` keeps its current behaviour and its single caller at :1253. The function name and its no-argument path (start check, :311, with its live base freshness through `fm_binding head` and the `authoritative PR head moved; refresh before review` message) are unchanged, so tests/external-execution.test.sh:229-244, which extracts the function by name and calls it with no argument, stays green unchanged. The no-argument path's REVIEW_PR_BASE clause (:306-309) becomes unreachable from the script once :819 passes `settled` (the start call runs before REVIEW_PR_BASE is set); remove that clause, so the no-argument path is: binding head, compare with R_HEAD. REVIEW_PR_BASE_HEAD then has no reader, which shellcheck (`bin/ci.sh:583`, `shellcheck -x -S warning`) would flag as SC2034: remove it from :287 (which becomes `REVIEW_PR_BASE=''`) and replace the assignment at :315 with `git rev-parse --verify -q "$BASE^{commit}" >/dev/null || exit 65`, which keeps today's refusal when the local base does not resolve. REVIEW_PR_BASE stays: the settled and final paths read it as --base-name. (2) When `verify_review_head settled` fails, fm-review prints one stderr line `fm-review: the PR changed while the review waited for CI; no review ran` after the binding's own `fm-binding: <reason>` line (which review-final already prints), emits `--review-outcome infrastructure_error --type review_failed --en 'PR head changed, retargeted or closed while the review waited for CI; no review ran' --tw '審核等待 CI 期間 PR 版本變更、改了 base 或已關閉；沒有執行審核'`, and exits 65 — the same outcome shape the final check uses at :1254-1258, without stale-final.txt (no answer exists yet). The reviewer adapter is never started on that path. (3) Comments at :284-286 and above :819 say: the start check requires a fresh base; the check after the CI wait and the final check bind the reviewed head and base name only (T-213, T-201).

Behaviour after the change, read against current code: main advancing (and firstmate fast-forwarding the local base) at any time after the start check no longer refuses the round; the round reviews R_BASE..R_HEAD pinned at :382-389 and records the verdict bound to them, as T-201's base-move case already does when main moves during the adapter. The start check is unchanged: a local base that is stale relative to the live base at launch still refuses with `fm-binding: local base is stale; synchronize before accepting` (fm_binding.py:275), which is loud and names the fix. A head that moved, a retargeted base name, a closed PR, a fetched PR head or local task ref that differs from R_HEAD, or an unreadable PR during the CI wait still refuses, now with the stderr lines and review_failed event of change (2). No new binding mode: `review-final` is reused as is (fm_binding.py is not edited).

Tests. (a) tests/review-verdict.test.sh, next to the T-201 movement loop (:663-718), a new loop `T-213: movement while the review waits for CI` with movements base, head, retarget, closed. Its fixture's gh stub (a copy of `ghstub` from tests/lib/review.sh:78-80 that logs calls the same way) answers the required-checks request fm-review sends first after preparation (`api repos/.../branches/<base>/protection/required_status_checks`, the same request tests/live-base-binding.test.sh's stub answers at :21-23) with `{"contexts":[],"checks":[]}` and, on that first request only, performs the movement exactly as the T-201 mock adapter does (:671-689): base = an unrelated commit on main via commit-tree/update-ref; head = the same on work; retarget = write `.fixture-pr-base`; closed = touch `.fixture-pr-closed`. The mock adapter writes `APPROVE:T-Z` and also touches `$FM_TARGET_ROOT/.adapter-ran`. Assertions: base → exit 0, `.adapter-ran` exists, the verdict record's head/base/patch equal the values computed before the run (as :697-703 do), the verdict is projected (`pr comment` in ghcalls) and `approved` is emitted, no stale-final.txt; head, retarget, closed → exit 65, `.adapter-ran` absent, no verdict record, no `pr comment`, the last review_failed event has review_outcome infrastructure_error and its en summary contains `while the review waited for CI`, stderr contains `fm-review: the PR changed while the review waited for CI` and `fm-binding:`, and no stale-final.txt exists. The base case is red on base (today it exits 65 silently); the head/retarget/closed cases' stderr/event assertions are red on base; their exit-65 and no-verdict assertions are regression guards. The existing T-201 loop (:663-718) stays unchanged and green. (b) tests/external-execution.test.sh: one new case that extracts verify_review_head as :230 does and calls `verify_review_head settled` with FM_EXTERNAL=1, TASK, PR=9, BRANCH, R_HEAD=reviewed, REVIEW_PR_BASE=main and a stub `fm_binding() { printf '%s\n' "$*" > "$CALLS"; printf reviewed; }`; it asserts exit 0 and that the recorded arguments begin with `review-final` and contain `--head reviewed --base-name main`; a second call with the stub printing `stale` asserts a non-zero exit. Red on base (no `settled` value: today it takes the no-argument path and calls `head`). (c) tests/herdr/credentials.py:149-155: the pinned fetch sequence changes because the check after the CI wait now fetches only the PR head. Replace the expectation with `pair * 2 + (pair + ['refs/heads/main']) + ['refs/pull/35/head'] * 2` and the comment with: the autopilot verifies twice; the review's start check fetches the PR head and the live base and reads the base; the checks after the CI wait and before publication run review-final, which fetches only the PR head. Grep tests/ for every other assertion on the number or order of binding fetches or on `fm_binding head`/`base` calls made by a full `fm-review.sh --pr` run (tests/local-round-loop.test.sh, tests/e2e-loop.test.sh, tests/decide.test.sh, tests/merge.test.sh, tests/selfupdate.test.sh, tests/conventions-publication.test.sh, tests/board-card-effects.test.sh, tests/lib/autopilot_turn.py all install binding_service_fixture from tests/lib/binding-fixture.sh, whose stub already answers review-final at :30-38) and update any that pins the old sequence; state in the PR which were checked. tests/live-base-binding.test.sh is unchanged (it calls fm_binding.py directly). (d) tests/codex-review-integration.test.sh:173-179 `test_ref_moved_during_ci_wait_refused_before_model` runs the real fm-review.sh and fm_binding.py; its gh stub moves refs/heads/work on the protection request during the CI wait (:86-90), and it asserts `authoritative PR head differs` (:177), text that came from `fm_binding head` at :819. After this change :819 runs review-final, which refuses that move with `local task ref differs from reviewed head` (fm_binding.py:148). Change only :177 to assert `local task ref differs from reviewed head` and add assertIn('fm-review: the PR changed while the review waited for CI', result.stderr); keep its exit-65, no-capture and not-published assertions. `test_remote_update_branch_refused_before_prompt_or_checkout` (:163-171) is the start check and stays unchanged. Correction to (a): on base the `closed` movement passes :819 (the fixture's head/base modes ignore .fixture-pr-closed) and fails only at the final check with stale-final.txt, so its `.adapter-ran`-absent and no-stale-final assertions are also red on base.

Docs, edited in place (T-189 rule; nothing appended at the end of design.md): design/design.md §15.7 'Portable roles and stock execution' (starts :5217): in the paragraph at about :5241-5243 change 'compares its authoritative head and fresh base with local refs before preparation and after the CI wait' to say it compares its authoritative head and fresh base with local refs before preparation, and after the CI wait binds the same things the final check binds (open PR, head equal to the reviewed head, fetched PR ref and local task ref, unchanged base name), so main moving during the CI wait does not void the round (T-213); in the paragraph at about :5298-5302 change 'before preparing review, after the CI wait and before publishing' so it says the stale-local-ref refusal holds before preparing review and the head/ref equality holds after the CI wait and before publishing. Name T-213 in both edits.

In flight and migration. No stored record, event type or file format changes; review_failed with review_outcome infrastructure_error already exists (used at :1254-1258), so fm-diagram ROUTINE and board readers need no change. Open PRs at the time of writing (#159 T-055, #198 T-209 and any later) are unaffected until their next review round, which runs the new script (sessions freeze engine code per session, §11; a round already running finishes on the old code). Gate 7 is untouched, so verdicts already recorded keep their meaning. External projects take the same path; review-final already serves them at the final check.

Workers do not run the suites. Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates. Fail-first is expected from tests/review-verdict.test.sh (the base case and the stderr/event assertions of the T-213 loop) and tests/external-execution.test.sh (the `settled` case); tests/herdr/credentials.py's new sequence and tests/codex-review-integration.test.sh's new stderr assertions at :177 are red on base. Stubs answer like the real tools: the required-checks response has GitHub's `contexts`/`checks` shape, and the movements are real git ref updates in the fixture repo, as in the T-201 loop.
